records.source: Ἐπειδήπερ πολλοὶ ἐπεχείρησαν ἀνατάξασθαι διήγησιν περὶ τῶν πεπληροφορημένων ἐν ἡμῖν πραγμάτων, καθὼς παρέδοσαν ἡμῖν οἱ ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς αὐτόπται καὶ ὑπηρέται γενόμενοι τοῦ λόγου, ἔδοξε κἀμοὶ παρηκολουθηκότι ἄνωθεν πᾶσιν ἀκριβῶς καθεξῆς σοι γράψαι, κράτιστε Θεόφιλε, ἵνα ἐπιγνῷς περὶ ὧν κατηχήθης λόγων τὴν ἀσφάλειαν.
records.gloss: Inasmuch as many have undertaken to draw up a narrative concerning the having been fully accomplished among us matters, \v 2 as delivered to us the [ones] from beginning eyewitnesses and servants having become of the word, \v 3 it seemed good also to me, having followed from the first all things accurately, in order to you to write, most excellent Theophilus, \v 4 so that you may know concerning which you were instructed words the certainty.
pieces: Many people have set their hands to putting together an account of the events that have been brought to completion among us.
They wrote them down as they were passed on to us by those who saw them from the beginning and became servants of the word.
So I too, having followed the whole course of things closely from the start, decided to write them out for you in order, most excellent Theophilus,
so that you can be sure of the things you were taught.

L.1: Since many have undertaken to compile a narrative about the matters that have been brought to completion among us,
L.2: just as those who from [the] beginning were eyewitnesses and became servants of the word handed [them] down to us,
L.3: it seemed good to me also, having followed all things accurately from the start, to write [them] in order for you, most excellent Theophilus,
L.4: so that you may know the certainty concerning the words in which you were instructed.

R.1: Dear Theophilus: Many people have tried to write down the story of the things that have happened among us.
R.2: They wrote what was told to us by people who saw these things from the beginning and who then served by spreading the message.
R.3: I have looked carefully into all of it from the very start. So I decided that I too should write it all down for you in a clear order,
R.4: so that you can know that what you were taught is true.

decisions.choice: one long sentence: a formal preface in the style of Greek historians
decisions.reason: Verses 1-4 are a single carefully built Greek sentence, the most polished in the New Testament. Writers of history began this way: they named earlier works, their sources, their own method and their reader. From 1:5 on Luke changes style and tells the story in the plain manner of the Greek Old Testament.

decisions.choice: brought to completion: events that have run their full course, and that God has brought to fulfillment
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "fully convinced" (Romans 4:21) or "fulfilled, carried out fully". With "matters" or "events" it means things that have taken place in full. Luke goes on to tell the story as the fulfillment of what God promised (1:20, 45; 24:44).

decisions.choice: eyewitnesses and servants of the word: one group, who saw the events and then served by preaching them
alternatives: two groups, eyewitnesses and later preachers
decisions.reason: One article governs both nouns, so the same people are meant. "The word" is the message about Jesus, as in Acts 6:4 and 8:4. Luke does not claim to be one of them; he received what they handed down.

decisions.choice: having followed from the start: having traced the events carefully from their beginning
decisions.reason: The adverb can mean "from above" (John 3:3) but here it means "from the first", matching "from the beginning" in 1:2. Luke has kept close track of the events, as a careful historian does.

decisions.choice: in order: an orderly, well-arranged account
decisions.reason: The word means in sequence or in order. Luke does not say the order is always the order of time; he means a connected, well-arranged account.

decisions.choice: most excellent Theophilus: a real person, addressed with a title of rank
alternatives: any lover of God, as the name means
decisions.reason: The name means "friend of God", but "most excellent" was a title for men of high rank, such as the Roman governors Felix and Festus (Acts 23:26; 26:25). Luke dedicates Acts to him too (Acts 1:1).

decisions.choice: instructed ... certainty: what Theophilus has been taught, and how firmly it stands
decisions.reason: The verb is used of teaching about the faith (Acts 18:25; Galatians 6:6). The last word of the sentence is "certainty", the reliability of what he was taught: Luke's whole purpose.

decisions.choice: Dear Theophilus (at the start)
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long sentence and names the reader at the start, as a modern letter does.

decisions.choice: the things you were taught (B); what you were taught (R)
alternatives: the words in which you were instructed
decisions.reason: "Words" here means the matters taught, not single words.

records.heading: An orderly account for Theophilus

records.source: Ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἡρῴδου βασιλέως τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἱερεύς τις ὀνόματι Ζαχαρίας ἐξ ἐφημερίας Ἀβιά, καὶ γυνὴ αὐτῷ ἐκ τῶν θυγατέρων Ἀαρών, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῆς Ἐλισάβετ.
records.gloss: There was in the days of Herod king of the Judea a priest certain by name Zechariah of [the] division of Abijah, and wife to him of the daughters of Aaron, and the name of her Elizabeth.
pieces: In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah, who belonged to the priestly division of Abijah. His wife was also descended from Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.

L.5: In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a certain priest named Zechariah, of the division of Abijah, and he had a wife from the daughters of Aaron, and her name [was] Elizabeth.

R.5: When Herod was king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah. He belonged to the group of priests called the division of Abijah. His wife Elizabeth also came from the family of Aaron, the first priest.

decisions.choice: there was: Luke begins his story in the style of the Greek Old Testament
alternatives: a plain past tense with no wider echo
decisions.reason: The opening "It came to pass in the days of ..." is how many Old Testament stories begin (Judges 13:2; 1 Samuel 1:1; Ruth 1:1). After the polished preface, Luke tells the birth stories in the language of Israel's Scriptures.

decisions.choice: Herod, king of Judea: Herod the Great, who ruled the Jewish land under Rome and died in 4 BC
decisions.reason: Rome gave Herod the title "king". Judea here means the whole land of the Jews, not only the southern district (compare 4:44; 23:5).

decisions.choice: the division of Abijah: one of the twenty-four groups of priests that took turns serving in the temple
alternatives: a family or clan name only
decisions.reason: King David divided the priests into twenty-four divisions; Abijah's was the eighth (1 Chronicles 24:10). Each division served in the temple for a week, about twice a year.

decisions.choice: from the daughters of Aaron: Elizabeth was herself of priestly descent
alternatives: a figure of speech for a godly woman
decisions.reason: Aaron was the first high priest, and all priests descended from him. A priest who married within the priestly line was especially honored.

decisions.choice: the first priest
decisions.reason: Readable says who Aaron was.

records.heading: Gabriel comes to Zechariah in the temple

records.source: ἦσαν δὲ δίκαιοι ἀμφότεροι ἐναντίον τοῦ θεοῦ, πορευόμενοι ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐντολαῖς καὶ δικαιώμασιν τοῦ κυρίου ἄμεμπτοι.
records.gloss: They were and righteous both before the God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.
pieces: Both of them were righteous in God's eyes, and they lived by every commandment and requirement of the Lord with no fault to be found in them.

L.6: And they were both righteous before God, walking blameless in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord.

R.6: Both of them did what was right in God's eyes. They obeyed all the Lord's commands and rules, and no one could find fault with them.

decisions.choice: righteous: living rightly before God, faithful to his law
alternatives: made right with God by faith
decisions.reason: The word describes their way of life, as the rest of the verse explains. It does not mean they never sinned; Zechariah will doubt the angel (1:20). Luke uses the same word for Simeon (2:25) and Joseph of Arimathea (23:50).

decisions.choice: commandments and ordinances: the whole law God gave Israel
alternatives: two different parts of the law
decisions.reason: The two words are paired in the Greek Old Testament for all that God requires (Genesis 26:5; Deuteronomy 4:40).

decisions.choice: blameless: no one could charge them with breaking the law
decisions.reason: The word is used of Job (Job 1:1) and of Paul's past keeping of the law (Philippians 3:6). It speaks of their visible conduct.

decisions.choice: lived by (B); obeyed (R)
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a Hebrew picture for how one lives. Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

decisions.choice: did what was right in God's eyes
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word. This is the adjective, not the key term "righteousness", which stays the same at every level.

records.source: καὶ οὐκ ἦν αὐτοῖς τέκνον, καθότι ἦν ἡ Ἐλισάβετ στεῖρα, καὶ ἀμφότεροι προβεβηκότες ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις αὐτῶν ἦσαν.
records.gloss: And not was to them a child, because was the Elizabeth barren, and both advanced in the days of them were.
pieces: But they had no children, because Elizabeth could not conceive, and both of them were getting on in years.

L.7: And they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in their days.

R.7: But they had no children, because Elizabeth was not able to have a baby. And now they were both very old.

decisions.choice: a childless couple, old and righteous: the pattern of Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel and Hannah
decisions.reason: Israel's Scriptures tell of barren women to whom God gave a son: Sarah (Genesis 18:11), Rebekah (25:21), Rachel (30:22-23), Samson's mother (Judges 13:2) and Hannah (1 Samuel 1:2). Luke's readers would expect God to act.

decisions.choice: barren: unable to bear children; in that culture often seen as a shame
alternatives: a judgment of God on her
decisions.reason: Childlessness was a deep sorrow and could be taken as a mark of disgrace (1:25). Luke has just said both were righteous, so it is not a punishment.

decisions.choice: advanced in their days: old
alternatives: in the later part of the day
decisions.reason: A Hebrew way of saying someone is old, used of Abraham and Sarah (Genesis 18:11).

records.source: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ ἱερατεύειν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ τάξει τῆς ἐφημερίας αὐτοῦ ἔναντι τοῦ θεοῦ κατὰ τὸ ἔθος τῆς ἱερατείας ἔλαχε τοῦ θυμιᾶσαι εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸν ναὸν τοῦ κυρίου, καὶ πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος ἦν τοῦ λαοῦ προσευχόμενον ἔξω τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦ θυμιάματος·
records.gloss: It came to pass then in the serving as priest him in the order of the division of him before the God, \v 9 according to the custom of the priesthood it fell by lot to him to burn incense having entered into the temple of the Lord, \v 10 and all the multitude was of the people praying outside at the hour of the incense;
pieces: Once, when Zechariah's division was on duty and he was serving as priest before God,
he was chosen by lot, as the custom of the priesthood was, to go into the sanctuary of the Lord and burn incense.
At the hour of the incense offering, the whole crowd of people was praying outside.

L.8: And it happened, while he was serving as priest before God in the order of his division,
L.9: according to the custom of the priesthood, it fell to him by lot to burn incense, having entered into the temple of the Lord.
L.10: And the whole multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of the incense.

R.8: One time Zechariah's group was on duty at the temple, and he was serving God there as a priest.
R.9: The priests always chose by lot who would go into the holy place of the Lord's temple to burn incense. This time Zechariah was chosen.
R.10: While the incense was being offered, a large crowd of people was outside, praying.

decisions.choice: it fell to him by lot to burn incense: a duty chosen by lot among the many priests, perhaps once in a lifetime
alternatives: a regular duty that came to him often
decisions.reason: There were many priests, and lots decided who would offer the incense on the golden altar inside the sanctuary (Exodus 30:7-8). Later Jewish tradition (the Mishnah, tractate Tamid) says a priest could do this only once in his life.

decisions.choice: the temple: the sanctuary building itself, which only priests could enter
alternatives: the whole temple area with its courts
decisions.reason: Luke uses a word for the inner building. The people stayed outside in the courts (1:10, 21).

decisions.choice: the hour of the incense: the time of the daily morning or evening offering, also a time of prayer
decisions.reason: Incense was burned every morning and evening (Exodus 30:7-8). The evening offering was a time of prayer (Acts 3:1; compare Psalm 141:2).

decisions.choice: sanctuary (B); holy place of the Lord's temple (R)
decisions.reason: In English "temple" suggests the whole complex. Balanced and Readable name the inner building Zechariah entered.

records.source: ὤφθη δὲ αὐτῷ ἄγγελος κυρίου ἑστὼς ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τοῦ θυμιάματος.
records.gloss: Appeared then to him an angel of [the] Lord standing at [the] right of the altar of the incense.
pieces: Then an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing to the right of the altar of incense.

L.11: And an angel of [the] Lord appeared to him, standing at [the] right [side] of the altar of incense.

R.11: Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared to Zechariah. The angel stood at the right side of the altar where the incense was burned.

decisions.choice: an angel of the Lord: a messenger sent from God
decisions.reason: In 1:19 the angel names himself Gabriel and says God sent him. "The Lord" here is God.

decisions.choice: the right side of the altar: the side of favor
decisions.reason: The right side was the place of honor and favor; the angel's place may already hint that the news is good.

decisions.choice: Suddenly
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the appearance was unexpected, as 1:12 makes clear.

records.source: καὶ ἐταράχθη Ζαχαρίας ἰδών, καὶ φόβος ἐπέπεσεν ἐπ’ αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And was troubled Zechariah having seen, and fear fell upon him.
pieces: When Zechariah saw him, he was shaken, and fear came over him.

L.12: And Zechariah was troubled when he saw [him], and fear fell upon him.

R.12: Zechariah was very upset when he saw the angel, and he was afraid.

decisions.choice: fear fell upon him: he was overcome with fear
decisions.reason: The fear of one who meets a messenger from God, as in Judges 6:22-23 and Daniel 8:17. Luke often tells of fear at God's appearing (1:65; 2:9; 5:26).

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ ἄγγελος· Μὴ φοβοῦ, Ζαχαρία, διότι εἰσηκούσθη ἡ δέησίς σου, καὶ ἡ γυνή σου Ἐλισάβετ γεννήσει υἱόν σοι, καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰωάννην·
records.gloss: Said then to him the angel, Not fear, Zechariah, because was heard the prayer of you, and the wife of you Elizabeth will bear a son to you, and you will call the name of him John;
pieces: But the angel said to him, "Do not be afraid, Zechariah. Your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will give you a son, and you are to name him John.

L.13: But the angel said to him, "Do not be afraid, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will call his name John.

R.13: But the angel told him, "Zechariah, do not be afraid! God has heard your prayer. Your wife Elizabeth will have a baby boy, and you must name him John.

decisions.choice: your prayer: most likely his prayer for a son, perhaps also his prayer as a priest for Israel
alternatives: only the prayer offered with the incense for the nation
decisions.reason: The angel at once promises a son, so the prayer heard is most naturally his long-standing request for a child. But Zechariah is praying in the temple at the hour of Israel's prayer, and the son will bring Israel back to God (1:16-17), so the two may be one answer.

decisions.choice: has been heard: God has heard it
decisions.reason: The passive leaves God unnamed, as Jewish speech often did.

decisions.choice: you will call his name John: God himself names the child
decisions.reason: The future is a command, as in Matthew 1:21. The name John means "the LORD has been gracious". Luke does not explain it, but the naming becomes a turning point in 1:59-64.

decisions.choice: God has heard your prayer
decisions.reason: Readable names God, whom the passive implies.

decisions.choice: you are to name him (B); you must name him (R)
decisions.reason: The future tense here gives a command; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: καὶ ἔσται χαρά σοι καὶ ἀγαλλίασις, καὶ πολλοὶ ἐπὶ τῇ γενέσει αὐτοῦ χαρήσονται·
records.gloss: And will be joy to you and gladness, and many at the birth of him will rejoice;
pieces: He will be your joy and delight, and many people will be glad that he was born.

L.14: And you will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth.

R.14: You will be full of joy and very happy, and many people will be glad because he has been born.

decisions.choice: joy and gladness: deep joy, the joy of celebration
decisions.reason: The two words say the same thing twice to make it strong. The second is the joy of worship and festival; the same word returns in 1:44 and 1:47.

decisions.choice: many will rejoice: the joy reaches beyond the family
decisions.reason: The joy at John's birth is fulfilled when neighbors and relatives rejoice with Elizabeth (1:58), and points to what he will do for Israel (1:16).

records.source: ἔσται γὰρ μέγας ἐνώπιον τοῦ κυρίου, καὶ οἶνον καὶ σίκερα οὐ μὴ πίῃ, καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου πλησθήσεται ἔτι ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ πολλοὺς τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ἐπιστρέψει ἐπὶ κύριον τὸν θεὸν αὐτῶν·
records.gloss: He will be for great before the Lord, and wine and strong drink not not he will drink, and of Spirit Holy he will be filled even from womb of mother of him, \v 16 and many of the sons of Israel he will turn to [the] Lord the God of them;
pieces: For he will be great in the sight of the Lord. He must never drink wine or beer, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even before he is born.
He will bring many of the people of Israel back to the Lord their God.

L.15: For he will be great before the Lord, and he will never drink wine or strong drink, and he will be filled with [the] Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb.
L.16: And he will turn many of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel to [the] Lord their God.

R.15: He will be great in the Lord's eyes. He must never drink wine or any other strong drink. Even before he is born he will be filled with the Holy Spirit.
R.16: He will lead many of the people of Israel to turn back to the Lord their God.

decisions.choice: never drink wine or strong drink: a life set apart for God, like a Nazirite
decisions.reason: The words echo the Nazirite vow (Numbers 6:3) and the charge given about Samson (Judges 13:4) and the priests on duty (Leviticus 10:9). The Greek says "not, not": never. Strong drink is beer or other drink made from grain or fruit.

decisions.choice: filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb: before his birth
alternatives: from the moment of his birth
decisions.reason: "Even from the womb" in the Greek Old Testament means before birth (Judges 13:5; Psalm 22:10). It is fulfilled when the unborn John leaps at Mary's greeting (1:41, 44).

decisions.choice: turn: bring back in repentance
decisions.reason: The verb is the prophets' word for turning back to God (Malachi 2:6; compare Luke 3:3, 8). John's work is to call Israel back to their God.

decisions.choice: beer (B); strong drink (R)
decisions.reason: In the ancient world strong drink was most often beer, made from barley; it was not distilled liquor. Readable keeps the general phrase.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: "Sons of Israel" means the Israelites, men and women. Literal keeps the Greek with a setting; Balanced and Readable use a word that is already inclusive.

decisions.choice: even before he is born
decisions.reason: Balanced says plainly what the Hebrew idiom means.

records.source: καὶ αὐτὸς προελεύσεται ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ ἐν πνεύματι καὶ δυνάμει Ἠλίου, ἐπιστρέψαι καρδίας πατέρων ἐπὶ τέκνα καὶ ἀπειθεῖς ἐν φρονήσει δικαίων, ἑτοιμάσαι κυρίῳ λαὸν κατεσκευασμένον.
records.gloss: And he will go before before him in spirit and power of Elijah, to turn hearts of fathers to children and disobedient [ones] to [the] wisdom of righteous [ones], to prepare for [the] Lord a people having been made ready.
pieces: He will go ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers back to their children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous, and so make ready a people prepared for the Lord."

L.17: And he will go before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in [the] spirit and power of Elijah, to turn [the] hearts of fathers to [their] children, and [the] disobedient to [the] wisdom of [the] righteous, to make ready for [the] Lord a prepared people."

R.17: He will go ahead of the Lord with the same spirit and power that Elijah the prophet had. He will bring fathers and their children back together. He will lead people who do not obey God to think the way good people do. He will get people ready for the Lord."

decisions.choice: before him: before the Lord their God of 1:16
alternatives: before the Messiah, who has not yet been named
decisions.reason: The nearest "him" is "the Lord their God" in 1:16. John goes ahead of God himself, as Malachi 3:1 says. Luke's readers will see that God comes in Jesus (1:43, 76).

decisions.choice: the spirit and power of Elijah ... turn the hearts of fathers to their children: Malachi 4:5-6
decisions.reason: Malachi ends with God's promise to send Elijah before the great day of the Lord, to turn the hearts of fathers to their children (Malachi 4:5-6; 3:23-24 in the Hebrew). John is not Elijah come back to life, but he comes with Elijah's spirit and power, to do Elijah's work.

decisions.choice: the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous: bringing those who do not obey God to think and live as the righteous do
decisions.reason: The second phrase interprets Malachi: the turning is a turning back to God's ways, not only a mending of families.

decisions.choice: to make ready a prepared people: the goal of all John's work
alternatives: a third task alongside the others
decisions.reason: The last phrase sums up the purpose: when the Lord comes, a people will be ready for him.

decisions.choice: the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable names the one meant by "him".

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν Ζαχαρίας πρὸς τὸν ἄγγελον· Κατὰ τί γνώσομαι τοῦτο;
records.gloss: And said Zechariah to the angel, By what will I know this?
pieces: Zechariah said to the angel, "How can I be sure of this?

L.18: And Zechariah said to the angel, "By what will I know this?

R.18: Zechariah asked the angel, "How can I know that this is true?

decisions.choice: by what will I know this: a request for proof
alternatives: a simple question how it will happen
decisions.reason: Zechariah asks for a sign, as Abraham did ("By what shall I know?", Genesis 15:8 in the Greek). Mary's question in 1:34 is different: she asks how, not for proof. The angel answers Zechariah with a sign that is also a discipline (1:20).

records.source: ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι πρεσβύτης καὶ ἡ γυνή μου προβεβηκυῖα ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: I for am an old man and the wife of me advanced in the days of her.
pieces: I am an old man, and my wife is getting on in years."

L.18: For I am an old man, and my wife [is] advanced in her days."

R.18: I am old, and my wife is old too."

decisions.choice: advanced in her days: old
decisions.reason: The same idiom as in 1:7.

records.source: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Γαβριὴλ ὁ παρεστηκὼς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ἀπεστάλην λαλῆσαι πρὸς σὲ καὶ εὐαγγελίσασθαί σοι ταῦτα·
records.gloss: And answering the angel said to him, I am Gabriel the [one] standing before the God, and I was sent to speak to you and to bring good news to you these [things];
pieces: The angel answered him, "I am Gabriel. I stand in the presence of God, and I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.

L.19: And answering, the angel said to him, "I am Gabriel, who stands before God, and I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.

R.19: The angel answered, "I am Gabriel. I stand in front of God and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He sent me to talk to you and to tell you this good news.

decisions.choice: Gabriel: the angel who explained God's plans to Daniel
decisions.reason: Gabriel appears in Daniel 8:16 and 9:21, where he brings understanding about the time of God's deliverance, at the hour of the evening offering (Daniel 9:21).

decisions.choice: who stands before God: one of the angels who serve in God's presence
alternatives: one who stands to be judged
decisions.reason: To stand before a king was to be one of his servants at court (1 Kings 10:8). Gabriel's rank gives weight to his words.

decisions.choice: bring good news: announce good news
alternatives: preach the gospel, in the later sense
decisions.reason: This is the verb from which the word for the gospel comes. Here it is the first of many uses in Luke (2:10; 4:18), for news of God's saving acts.

decisions.choice: bring you this good news
decisions.reason: The verb means to announce good news. "Preach" would make it sound like a sermon.

decisions.choice: He sent me
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the sender.

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἔσῃ σιωπῶν καὶ μὴ δυνάμενος λαλῆσαι ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας γένηται ταῦτα, ἀνθ’ ὧν οὐκ ἐπίστευσας τοῖς λόγοις μου, οἵτινες πληρωθήσονται εἰς τὸν καιρὸν αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And behold you will be silent and not being able to speak until which day happen these [things], because not you believed the words of me, which will be fulfilled in the time of them.
pieces: And now you will be silent, unable to speak, until the day these things take place, because you did not believe my words. They will come true at their proper time."

L.20: And look, you will be silent and not able to speak until the day these things happen, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their time."

R.20: But you did not believe what I told you. So now you will not be able to speak until the day all this happens. Everything I said will come true at the right time."

decisions.choice: you will be silent: the sign Zechariah asked for, and a discipline for his unbelief
decisions.reason: Zechariah asked how he could know (1:18). The silence answers him: it is the sign, and it is also the consequence of not believing. It ends when he obeys the angel's word about the name (1:63-64).

decisions.choice: in their time: at the time God has set
decisions.reason: The word means the appointed time. God's word will be fulfilled when he has planned.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: the reason first: "But you did not believe ... So now ..."
decisions.reason: Readable puts the cause before the result, which is easier to follow.

records.source: Καὶ ἦν ὁ λαὸς προσδοκῶν τὸν Ζαχαρίαν, καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ἐν τῷ χρονίζειν ἐν τῷ ναῷ αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And was the people waiting for the Zechariah, and they were wondering at the delaying in the temple him.
pieces: Meanwhile the people were waiting for Zechariah and wondering why he was staying so long in the sanctuary.

L.21: And the people were waiting for Zechariah, and they were wondering at his delaying in the temple.

R.21: Meanwhile, the people outside were waiting for Zechariah. They wondered why he was staying inside the temple so long.

decisions.choice: they wondered at his delay: the priest was expected to come out soon
decisions.reason: After burning the incense the priest came out to bless the people (compare Numbers 6:24-26). A long delay could make people fear that something had gone wrong in God's presence.

decisions.choice: sanctuary
decisions.reason: As in 1:9, the inner building.

records.source: ἐξελθὼν δὲ οὐκ ἐδύνατο λαλῆσαι αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν ὅτι ὀπτασίαν ἑώρακεν ἐν τῷ ναῷ· καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν διανεύων αὐτοῖς, καὶ διέμενεν κωφός.
records.gloss: Having come out then not he was able to speak to them, and they realized that a vision he had seen in the temple; and he was making signs to them, and remained mute.
pieces: When he came out, he could not speak to them, and they realized that he had seen a vision in the sanctuary. He kept making signs to them, but he remained unable to speak.

L.22: And when he came out, he was not able to speak to them, and they realized that he had seen a vision in the temple; and he kept making signs to them, and remained mute.

R.22: When he finally came out, he could not speak to them. They understood that he had seen a vision inside the temple. He kept using his hands to show them what he meant, but he could not say a word.

decisions.choice: mute: unable to speak, and perhaps also unable to hear
decisions.reason: The word can mean mute or deaf or both (7:22; 11:14). In 1:62 people make signs to him rather than speak, which suggests he could not hear either.

decisions.choice: sanctuary
decisions.reason: As in 1:9.

records.source: καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τῆς λειτουργίας αὐτοῦ, ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And it came to pass as were fulfilled the days of the service of him, he went away to the house of him.
pieces: When his days of service were over, he went home.

L.23: And it happened, when the days of his service were completed, he went away to his home.

R.23: When his time of work at the temple was finished, Zechariah went back home.

decisions.choice: service: his priestly duty in the temple
decisions.reason: The word was used for public service and, in the Greek Old Testament, for the service of priests and Levites (Numbers 8:22). His week of duty (1:5) ended.

decisions.choice: his home: in the hill country of Judea
decisions.reason: Many priests lived outside Jerusalem and came to the city when their division served. Mary visits him in a town in the hill country of Judah (1:39).

records.source: Μετὰ δὲ ταύτας τὰς ἡμέρας συνέλαβεν Ἐλισάβετ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ· καὶ περιέκρυβεν ἑαυτὴν μῆνας πέντε, λέγουσα ὅτι Οὕτως μοι πεποίηκεν κύριος ἐν ἡμέραις αἷς ἐπεῖδεν ἀφελεῖν ὄνειδός μου ἐν ἀνθρώποις.
records.gloss: After then these the days conceived Elizabeth the wife of him; and she hid herself months five, saying, \v 25 Thus to me has done [the] Lord in days in which he looked upon to take away reproach of me among men.
pieces: After this his wife Elizabeth became pregnant, and for five months she stayed in seclusion.
"The Lord has done this for me," she said. "In these days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has looked on me with favor and taken away my disgrace among {{gender:people|men}}."

L.24: And after these days Elizabeth his wife conceived, and she kept herself hidden five months, saying,
L.25: "Thus [the] Lord has done for me in [the] days when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} looked upon [me] to take away my disgrace among {{gender:people|men}}."

R.24: Soon after that, Zechariah's wife Elizabeth became pregnant. For five months she did not go out where people could see her.
R.25: She said, "The Lord has done this for me! He has been kind to me. Now people will no longer look down on me."

decisions.choice: she kept herself hidden five months: she stayed out of public view
alternatives: she was ashamed of the pregnancy
decisions.reason: Luke does not say why. Perhaps she waited until her pregnancy could be seen, so that people would believe what God had done; in 1:26 and 1:36 the sixth month becomes the sign given to Mary.

decisions.choice: to take away my disgrace: the words of Rachel at the birth of Joseph
decisions.reason: When God gave Rachel a son she said, "God has taken away my disgrace" (Genesis 30:23). Childlessness was seen as a shame; now God has ended it.

decisions.choice: looked upon: looked with favor and care
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God watching over someone to help (Acts 4:29).

decisions.choice: stayed in seclusion (B); did not go out where people could see her (R)
decisions.reason: "Hid herself" suggests fear. Balanced and Readable say what she did without suggesting a reason Luke does not give.

records.source: Ἐν δὲ τῷ μηνὶ τῷ ἕκτῳ ἀπεστάλη ὁ ἄγγελος Γαβριὴλ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς πόλιν τῆς Γαλιλαίας ᾗ ὄνομα Ναζαρὲθ πρὸς παρθένον ἐμνηστευμένην ἀνδρὶ ᾧ ὄνομα Ἰωσὴφ ἐξ οἴκου Δαυὶδ, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τῆς παρθένου Μαριάμ.
records.gloss: In then the month the sixth was sent the angel Gabriel from the God to a city of the Galilee to which name Nazareth \v 27 to a virgin betrothed to a man to whom name Joseph of house of David, and the name of the virgin Mary.
pieces: In the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent by God to Nazareth, a town of Galilee,
to a virgin who was engaged to Joseph, a man of the house of David. Her name was Mary.

L.26: And in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth,
L.27: to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name [was] Joseph, of [the] house of David, and the name of the virgin [was] Mary.

R.26: When Elizabeth was in her sixth month, God sent the angel Gabriel to the town of Nazareth in Galilee.
R.27: He was sent to a virgin named Mary. She was engaged to marry Joseph, who came from the family of King David.

decisions.choice: the sixth month: of Elizabeth's pregnancy
alternatives: the sixth month of the year
decisions.reason: The count follows from 1:24 and is confirmed in 1:36.

decisions.choice: Nazareth in Galilee: a small village in the north, far from Jerusalem and the temple
decisions.reason: The word can mean any town, large or small. Nazareth was an obscure village, never named in the Old Testament (compare John 1:46). The contrast with the temple scene of 1:8-23 is deliberate.

decisions.choice: virgin: a young woman who has not had sexual relations
alternatives: a young woman of marriageable age, with no claim about virginity
decisions.reason: The word can mean a young unmarried woman, but its usual sense is a virgin, and Mary's own question in 1:34 makes that the meaning here. Luke says it twice.

decisions.choice: betrothed: legally pledged to marry, but not yet living together
decisions.reason: A Jewish betrothal was a binding contract that only divorce could end (compare Matthew 1:18-19). The bride usually stayed in her father's house for up to a year before the wedding.

decisions.choice: of the house of David: Joseph's descent
decisions.reason: The phrase stands next to Joseph's name. Luke traces Jesus's royal line through Joseph, his legal father (2:4; 3:23), as the angel's promise of David's throne requires (1:32).

decisions.choice: engaged
decisions.reason: "Betrothed" is an old word. "Engaged" is the nearest modern word, and the meaning decision says how much more binding it was.

decisions.choice: When Elizabeth was in her sixth month
decisions.reason: Readable says whose sixth month it was (see the meaning decision).

records.heading: Gabriel comes to Mary in Nazareth

records.source: καὶ εἰσελθὼν πρὸς αὐτὴν εἶπεν· Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, ὁ κύριος μετὰ σοῦ.
records.gloss: And having come in to her he said, Rejoice, having been favored [one], the Lord with you.
pieces: He came to her and said, "Greetings! God has shown you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} favor. The Lord is with you."

L.28: And coming in to her, he said, "Greetings, you who have been favored! The Lord [is] with you."

R.28: The angel went to her and said, "Greetings! God has been very kind to you. The Lord is with you."

decisions.choice: greetings: the ordinary greeting, with an undertone of "rejoice"
decisions.reason: The word was the everyday Greek greeting, literally "rejoice". The prophets used it to call Zion to rejoice at God's coming (Zephaniah 3:14; Zechariah 9:9 in the Greek), and joy runs through this chapter, so some hear more than a greeting.

decisions.choice: favored one: one to whom God has shown grace
alternatives: full of grace, a fullness of grace she has to give
decisions.reason: The verb means to show grace or favor to someone; Ephesians 1:6 uses it of God's grace to all believers. The perfect participle says God has favored her. The Latin Vulgate's "full of grace" is not what the Greek says.

decisions.choice: the Lord is with you: a statement of God's presence
alternatives: a wish, "may the Lord be with you"
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb. With an angel's announcement it is a statement, as when the angel greets Gideon (Judges 6:12).

decisions.choice: the greeting ends with "with you", the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: many later manuscripts add "blessed are you among women"
decisions.reason: The added words come from Elizabeth's greeting in 1:42. Early manuscripts do not have them here. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: God has shown you his favor (B); God has been very kind to you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who has favored her and what the title means.

records.source: ἡ δὲ ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ διεταράχθη καὶ διελογίζετο ποταπὸς εἴη ὁ ἀσπασμὸς οὗτος.
records.gloss: She and at the word was greatly troubled and was considering what kind might be the greeting this.
pieces: His words disturbed her deeply, and she kept asking herself what such a greeting could mean.

L.29: But she was greatly troubled at the statement, and she was considering what kind of greeting this might be.

R.29: Mary was very upset by what the angel said. She wondered what this greeting could mean.

decisions.choice: greatly troubled: thoroughly shaken
alternatives: frightened only by the sight of the angel
decisions.reason: The verb is stronger than the one used of Zechariah (1:12). Luke says she was troubled by the words, not by the sight.

decisions.choice: she was considering: she kept thinking it over
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense shows an ongoing, inward reflection, as in 2:19 and 2:51.

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ ἄγγελος αὐτῇ· Μὴ φοβοῦ, Μαριάμ, εὗρες γὰρ χάριν παρὰ τῷ θεῷ·
records.gloss: And said the angel to her, Not fear, Mary, you found for grace with the God;
pieces: The angel said to her, "Do not be afraid, Mary. You have found favor with God.

L.30: And the angel said to her, "Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found grace with God.

R.30: The angel told her, "Mary, do not be afraid. God is pleased with you.

decisions.choice: you have found grace with God: God looks on you with favor
decisions.reason: An Old Testament phrase for being accepted by God (Genesis 6:8, of Noah). The favor is God's free gift, as "favored one" in 1:28 says.

decisions.choice: favor (B); God is pleased with you (R); grace (L)
decisions.reason: The key term is "grace", and Literal keeps it. But "found grace with" is not natural English; "found favor with" is the English idiom for the same thing. Readable says plainly what it means.

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ συλλήμψῃ ἐν γαστρὶ καὶ τέξῃ υἱόν, καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν.
records.gloss: And behold you will conceive in womb and will bear a son, and you will call the name of him Jesus.
pieces: You will become pregnant and have a son, and you are to give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the name Jesus.

L.31: And look, you will conceive in [your] womb and give birth to a son, and you will call {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name Jesus.

R.31: You will become pregnant and have a baby boy. You must name {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} Jesus.

decisions.choice: conceive and bear a son: an echo of Isaiah 7:14
decisions.reason: The words are close to Isaiah 7:14 in the Greek, which Matthew quotes (Matthew 1:23). Luke does not quote it but the virgin of 1:27 and these words recall it.

decisions.choice: you will call his name Jesus: the name is given by God
decisions.reason: Jesus is the Greek form of Joshua, "the LORD saves". As with John (1:13), God chooses the name. Here Mary is told to give it; in Matthew 1:21 Joseph is.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

records.source: οὗτος ἔσται μέγας καὶ υἱὸς Ὑψίστου κληθήσεται, καὶ δώσει αὐτῷ κύριος ὁ θεὸς τὸν θρόνον Δαυὶδ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ βασιλεύσει ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον Ἰακὼβ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, καὶ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔσται τέλος.
records.gloss: This will be great and son of Most High will be called, and will give to him [the] Lord the God the throne of David the father of him, \v 33 and he will reign over the house of Jacob to the ages, and of the kingdom of him not will be an end.
pieces: He will be great, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be called Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the throne of David, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} forefather,
and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be king over the house of Jacob for all ages. There will be no end to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom."

L.32: He will be great and will be called Son of [the] Most High, and [the] Lord God will give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the throne of David {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} father,
L.33: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom there will be no end."

R.32: He will be great. People will call {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the Son of God Most High. The Lord God will make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} king, as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ancestor David was.
R.33: He will rule over the people of Israel forever, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom will never end."

decisions.choice: the throne of David ... no end: God's promise to David in 2 Samuel 7
decisions.reason: God promised David a son whose throne and kingdom would last forever, and said, "I will be his father, and he will be my son" (2 Samuel 7:12-16; compare Isaiah 9:7). The angel says Jesus is that king.

decisions.choice: Son of the Most High: a title for the promised king, and more
alternatives: a title for any godly person
decisions.reason: "The Most High" is a name for God (Genesis 14:18-20). In the setting of 2 Samuel 7 the title marks the royal son; 1:35 explains that Jesus is God's Son in a deeper way, by his conception.

decisions.choice: David his father: his ancestor
alternatives: his father in the ordinary sense
decisions.reason: "Father" often means ancestor. Jesus is of David's line through Joseph (1:27).

decisions.choice: the house of Jacob: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Jacob, also named Israel, was the father of the twelve tribes.

decisions.choice: he: "this one", the son just named
decisions.reason: The pronoun points to the son of 1:31. Of John the angel said he would be great "before the Lord" (1:15); of Jesus he says simply "great", and names him Son of the Most High.

decisions.choice: forefather
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that "father" means ancestor here.

decisions.choice: make him king, as his ancestor David was; the people of Israel
alternatives: give him the throne of David his father; the house of Jacob
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pictures mean.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ Μαριὰμ πρὸς τὸν ἄγγελον· Πῶς ἔσται τοῦτο, ἐπεὶ ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω;
records.gloss: Said then Mary to the angel, How will be this, since a man not I know?
pieces: Mary said to the angel, "How can this happen? I have never been with a man."

L.34: And Mary said to the angel, "How will this be, since I do not know a man?"

R.34: Mary asked the angel, "How can this happen? I am a virgin."

decisions.choice: I do not know a man: I have not had sexual relations with a man
alternatives: I am not acquainted with any man
decisions.reason: "Know" is the Hebrew way of speaking of sexual union (Genesis 4:1; Matthew 1:25). Mary says she is a virgin.

decisions.choice: how will this be: a question about the way it will happen, not a doubt
alternatives: a request for proof like Zechariah's
decisions.reason: Zechariah asked how he could know (1:18) and was silenced; Mary asks how it will come about, and the angel explains (1:35). Elizabeth praises her for believing (1:45).

decisions.choice: since I do not know a man: she is a virgin, and the promise is for now, before her marriage
alternatives: a vow never to have relations with a man
decisions.reason: Mary is engaged to Joseph (1:27), so a child after the wedding would raise no question. She understands the angel to mean that she will conceive before she lives with Joseph. The present tense states her condition; it does not imply a vow.

decisions.choice: I have never been with a man (B); I am a virgin (R)
alternatives: I do not know a man
decisions.reason: In English "know" does not carry the Hebrew sense; Balanced and Readable say what Mary means.

records.source: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐπελεύσεται ἐπὶ σέ, καὶ δύναμις Ὑψίστου ἐπισκιάσει σοι· διὸ καὶ τὸ γεννώμενον ἅγιον κληθήσεται, υἱὸς θεοῦ·
records.gloss: And answering the angel said to her, [The] Spirit Holy will come upon you, and power of Most High will overshadow you; therefore also the being born holy will be called, son of God;
pieces: The angel answered her, "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will cover you with its shadow. So the child to be born will be holy, and will be called the Son of God.

L.35: And answering, the angel said to her, "[The] Holy Spirit will come upon you, and [the] power of [the] Most High will overshadow you; therefore also the holy one being born will be called Son of God.

R.35: The angel answered, "The Holy Spirit will come to you, and the power of God Most High will cover you like a cloud. So the baby will be holy. He will be called the Son of God.

decisions.choice: overshadow: God's presence resting on her, as the cloud rested on the tent of meeting
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the cloud of God's glory that covered the tabernacle (Exodus 40:35 in the Greek) and of the cloud at the transfiguration (9:34). Nothing in it suggests a physical union; the child comes from God's creative power.

decisions.choice: the child to be born will be called holy, the Son of God
alternatives: the holy one to be born will be called the Son of God
decisions.reason: "Holy" can go with "the one being born" (the holy child) or be what he will be called. Both are possible; either way he is holy and the Son of God. Balanced and Readable make "holy" a statement about the child; Literal keeps the Greek order.

decisions.choice: therefore: because his conception is the work of God's Spirit, he will be called God's Son
alternatives: he becomes Son of God only because of this birth
decisions.reason: The angel gives a reason linked to how he will be conceived. Luke does not say this is the only sense in which Jesus is God's Son (compare 3:22; 10:22).

decisions.choice: the one being born, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: some manuscripts add "of you": the one born of you
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts add "of you". Most early manuscripts do not. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: cover you with its shadow (B); cover you like a cloud (R)
decisions.reason: "Overshadow" in English usually means to outshine. Balanced and Readable keep the picture of a shadow or cloud resting on her.

decisions.choice: God Most High
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that "the Most High" is God.

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ Ἐλισάβετ ἡ συγγενίς σου καὶ αὐτὴ συνείληφεν υἱὸν ἐν γήρει αὐτῆς, καὶ οὗτος μὴν ἕκτος ἐστὶν αὐτῇ τῇ καλουμένῃ στείρᾳ·
records.gloss: And behold Elizabeth the relative of you also she has conceived a son in old age of her, and this month sixth is to her the [one] called barren;
pieces: Your relative Elizabeth, too, has conceived a son in her old age. People called her barren, yet this is her sixth month.

L.36: And look, Elizabeth your relative, she too has conceived a son in her old age, and this is [the] sixth month for her who was called barren.

R.36: Your relative Elizabeth is very old, and people said she could never have a baby. But she is going to have a son, and she is already six months pregnant.

decisions.choice: your relative: a family member, the exact relationship unknown
decisions.reason: The word means a kinswoman. Luke does not say how Mary and Elizabeth were related; "cousin" says more than the Greek.

decisions.choice: a sign given without being asked
decisions.reason: Mary did not ask for a sign as Zechariah did, but the angel gives her one: what God has done for Elizabeth shows what he can do.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20 and 1:31, the angel points to something new. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: people said she could never have a baby
decisions.reason: As in 1:7, the plain meaning of the word.

records.source: ὅτι οὐκ ἀδυνατήσει παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ πᾶν ῥῆμα.
records.gloss: For not will be impossible with the God every word.
pieces: For with God, no promise will prove impossible."

L.37: For no word from God will be impossible."

decisions.choice: an echo of God's words to Abraham about Sarah
decisions.reason: When Sarah laughed at the promise of a son in her old age, God said, "Is anything impossible for the LORD?" (Genesis 18:14). The Greek Old Testament there uses the same verb and the same noun. Luke sets Elizabeth, and now Mary, in Sarah's story.

decisions.choice: word: what God has spoken, and so the thing he has said will happen
decisions.reason: The noun can mean a spoken word or a matter. Here it holds both: nothing God says will fail to happen. Mary answers with the same noun in 1:38: "according to your word".

decisions.choice: will not be impossible with God: "from God" goes with the word, or with the power
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean that no word coming from God will lack power, or that nothing is impossible on God's part. Both say the same in the end.

decisions.choice: no promise will prove impossible (B); can do anything he says (R)
decisions.reason: "No word will be impossible" is awkward in English. Balanced calls the word a promise, as the context shows it is; Readable says the same thing positively.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ Μαριάμ· Ἰδοὺ ἡ δούλη κυρίου· γένοιτό μοι κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου.
records.gloss: Said then Mary, Behold the slave of [the] Lord; may it be to me according to the word of you.
pieces: Mary said, "I am the Lord's servant. Let it happen to me as you have said."

L.38: And Mary said, "Look, the slave of [the] Lord; may it happen to me according to your word."

R.38: Mary said, "I belong to the Lord, and I am ready to do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants. Let everything you said happen to me."

decisions.choice: slave: a woman who belongs to her master and is at his disposal
decisions.reason: The word is the feminine of the word for a slave (Philippians 2:7). Mary calls herself the Lord's slave: she belongs to him and puts herself at his command. Her place is that of one who belongs to a master, not of one in paid employment.

decisions.choice: may it happen to me: a wish and an act of consent
decisions.reason: The rare optative mood expresses a wish. Mary gives herself to God's purpose. "Word" is the same noun as in 1:37.

decisions.choice: I am (B); not rendered (R); look (L)
decisions.reason: Here the word means "here I am": Mary presents herself. Balanced says "I am".

decisions.choice: I belong to the Lord, and I am ready to do what he wants
decisions.reason: Readable explains what being the Lord's servant means for Mary here. This explains the word; the meaning decision gives the word itself.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that she belongs to the Lord, and Literal keeps "slave". Readable explains the word instead (r-en-2).

records.source: καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ἀπ’ αὐτῆς ὁ ἄγγελος.
records.gloss: And went away from her the angel.
pieces: Then the angel left her.

L.38: And the angel departed from her.

records.source: Ἀναστᾶσα δὲ Μαριὰμ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἐπορεύθη εἰς τὴν ὀρεινὴν μετὰ σπουδῆς εἰς πόλιν Ἰούδα, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον Ζαχαρίου καὶ ἠσπάσατο τὴν Ἐλισάβετ.
records.gloss: Having arisen then Mary in the days these went into the hill country with haste to a city of Judah, \v 40 and entered into the house of Zechariah and greeted the Elizabeth.
pieces: In those days Mary set out and hurried to a town in the hill country of Judah.
She went into Zechariah's house and greeted Elizabeth.

L.39: And in these days Mary arose and went with haste into the hill country, to a city of Judah,
L.40: and she entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.

R.39: Soon after this, Mary set off quickly for a town in the hills of Judah.
R.40: She went into Zechariah's house and said hello to Elizabeth.

decisions.choice: a town of Judah in the hill country: south of Jerusalem, about 80 to 100 miles from Nazareth
decisions.reason: Luke does not name the town. Judah's hill country lies around and south of Jerusalem. The journey from Nazareth took several days.

decisions.choice: having arisen: she got ready to go
decisions.reason: A Hebrew-style way of saying someone set out (15:18, 20).

decisions.choice: with haste: eagerly, without delay
decisions.reason: She goes at once to see the sign the angel gave her (1:36).

records.heading: Elizabeth greets the mother of her Lord

records.source: καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἤκουσεν τὸν ἀσπασμὸν τῆς Μαρίας ἡ Ἐλισάβετ, ἐσκίρτησεν τὸ βρέφος ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐπλήσθη πνεύματος ἁγίου ἡ Ἐλισάβετ, καὶ ἀνεφώνησεν κραυγῇ μεγάλῃ καὶ εἶπεν· Εὐλογημένη σὺ ἐν γυναιξίν, καὶ εὐλογημένος ὁ καρπὸς τῆς κοιλίας σου.
records.gloss: And it came to pass as heard the greeting of the Mary the Elizabeth, leaped the baby in the womb of her, and was filled of Spirit Holy the Elizabeth, \v 42 and she cried out with a cry loud and said, Blessed [are] you among women, and blessed the fruit of the womb of you.
pieces: As Mary's greeting reached Elizabeth, the child in her womb leaped, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
She cried out in a loud voice, "Of all women, you are the most blessed, and blessed is the child you carry!

L.41: And it happened, when Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the baby leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with [the] Holy Spirit,
L.42: and she called out with a loud cry and said, "Blessed [are] you among women, and blessed [is] the fruit of your womb!

R.41: As soon as Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the baby inside her jumped. And Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
R.42: She called out loudly, "God has blessed you more than any other woman! And God has blessed the baby you will have!

decisions.choice: the baby leaped: the unborn John moves, and Elizabeth takes it as joy (1:44)
alternatives: an ordinary movement with no meaning
decisions.reason: The angel said John would be filled with the Holy Spirit before birth (1:15). Elizabeth explains in 1:44 that he leaped for joy. The verb is used in Genesis 25:22 (Greek) of the twins in Rebekah's womb.

decisions.choice: blessed among women: the most blessed of all women
decisions.reason: Hebrew expresses the highest degree this way. Jael (Judges 5:24) is praised with similar words.

decisions.choice: the fruit of your womb: your child
decisions.reason: A Hebrew phrase for children (Deuteronomy 28:4).

decisions.choice: blessed: blessed by God
decisions.reason: The participle means having received God's blessing. A different word, "happy" or "blessed" in the sense of fortunate, comes in 1:45.

decisions.choice: the child you carry (B); the baby you will have (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means. The child is still in Mary's womb.

decisions.choice: God has blessed
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who blesses.

records.source: καὶ πόθεν μοι τοῦτο ἵνα ἔλθῃ ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ κυρίου μου πρὸς ἐμέ;
records.gloss: And from where to me this that should come the mother of the Lord of me to me?
pieces: Who am I, that the mother of my Lord should come to visit me?

L.43: And from where [does] this [come] to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?

R.43: Why should God be so good to me? The mother of my Lord has come to visit me!

decisions.choice: my Lord: Elizabeth calls Mary's unborn child her Lord
decisions.reason: In this chapter "the Lord" is God again and again (1:6, 9, 11, 15-17, 25, 28, 38). Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit (1:41), now uses the word of the child Mary carries. Luke calls Jesus "the Lord" in his own narrative (7:13; 10:1).

decisions.choice: from where is this to me: why am I given such an honor?
alternatives: a question about where Mary came from
decisions.reason: A humble question: she does not deserve the visit. Compare David's words in 2 Samuel 6:9, "How can the ark of the LORD come to me?"

decisions.choice: Who am I (B); Why should God be so good to me? (R)
alternatives: Why is this granted to me?
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the humble question in English idiom.

records.source: ἰδοὺ γὰρ ὡς ἐγένετο ἡ φωνὴ τοῦ ἀσπασμοῦ σου εἰς τὰ ὦτά μου, ἐσκίρτησεν ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει τὸ βρέφος ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ μου.
records.gloss: Behold for as came the sound of the greeting of you into the ears of me, leaped in gladness the baby in the womb of me.
pieces: The moment your greeting reached my ears, the child in my womb leaped with delight.

L.44: For look, as the sound of your greeting came into my ears, the baby in my womb leaped with gladness.

R.44: As soon as I heard your voice, the baby inside me jumped because he was so happy.

decisions.choice: with gladness: with the joy of celebration
decisions.reason: The noun is the gladness promised at John's birth (1:14) and the word of Mary's song (1:47). Even before birth John greets the Lord.

decisions.choice: look, for (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: Elizabeth points to what has just happened; Balanced and Readable carry it in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: καὶ μακαρία ἡ πιστεύσασα ὅτι ἔσται τελείωσις τοῖς λελαλημένοις αὐτῇ παρὰ κυρίου.
records.gloss: And blessed the [one] having believed that will be fulfillment to the things having been spoken to her from [the] Lord.
pieces: Blessed is the woman who believed that what the Lord said to her would be carried out!"

L.45: And blessed [is] she who believed that there will be a fulfillment of the things spoken to her from [the] Lord."

R.45: You are blessed, because you believed that the Lord would do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you!"

decisions.choice: blessed: fortunate, in a happy state because of God's favor
alternatives: blessed by God, the word of 1:42
decisions.reason: This is the word of the Beatitudes (6:20-22), not the participle of 1:42. It declares her fortunate. Mary takes it up in 1:48.

decisions.choice: that: what she believed
alternatives: because: she is blessed because the promise will be fulfilled
decisions.reason: The word can give the content of her faith or the reason she is blessed. Both make sense; the first follows the verb "believe" most naturally.

decisions.choice: she who believed: Mary, spoken of in the third person
alternatives: a general saying about anyone who believes
decisions.reason: Elizabeth speaks to Mary but praises her in the third person, as a blessing is often pronounced. Her faith stands against Zechariah's unbelief (1:20).

decisions.choice: You are blessed, because you believed
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to Mary directly, as Elizabeth is speaking to her.

records.source: Καὶ εἶπεν Μαριάμ· Μεγαλύνει ἡ ψυχή μου τὸν κύριον, καὶ ἠγαλλίασεν τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐπὶ τῷ θεῷ τῷ σωτῆρί μου·
records.gloss: And said Mary, Magnifies the soul of me the Lord, \v 47 and rejoiced the spirit of me in the God the Savior of me;
pieces: And Mary said, "My soul declares the greatness of the Lord,
and my spirit has found its delight in God my Savior,

L.46: And Mary said, "My soul magnifies the Lord,
L.47: and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,

R.46: Then Mary said, "With all my heart I praise the Lord.
R.47: I am so glad because God is my Savior.

decisions.choice: magnifies: declares how great the Lord is
decisions.reason: The verb means to make great, and so to praise as great. Mary cannot add to God's greatness; she proclaims it.

decisions.choice: my soul ... my spirit: my whole self
alternatives: two different parts of a person
decisions.reason: Hebrew poetry says one thing twice in parallel lines. Soul and spirit mean Mary herself, with all her being.

decisions.choice: Mary's song echoes Hannah's song (1 Samuel 2:1-10) and the Psalms
alternatives: a song with no Old Testament roots
decisions.reason: Hannah, another woman given a son by God, sang "My heart rejoices in the LORD" (1 Samuel 2:1). Almost every line of Mary's song (1:46-55) uses the words of Scripture: compare Psalm 35:9 and Habakkuk 3:18 for "rejoice in God my Savior".

decisions.choice: Mary, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Elizabeth, the reading of a few Latin manuscripts
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts give the song to Mary. A few Latin witnesses read "Elizabeth". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: has rejoiced: a past tense beside a present
alternatives: a different time from the first line
decisions.reason: The second verb is in the aorist, the first in the present. In Hebrew-style poetry the two lines say the same thing; the aorist may look back to the moment of the announcement.

decisions.choice: With all my heart
decisions.reason: Readable says what the parallel lines mean: Mary praises God with her whole self.

records.heading: Mary praises the Mighty One

records.source: ὅτι ἐπέβλεψεν ἐπὶ τὴν ταπείνωσιν τῆς δούλης αὐτοῦ, ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν μακαριοῦσίν με πᾶσαι αἱ γενεαί·
records.gloss: Because he looked upon the low state of the slave of him, behold for from the now will call blessed me all the generations;
pieces: because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has looked with care on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant in her lowly state. From this day people of every generation will call me blessed,

L.48: because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has looked upon the low position of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slave. For look, from now on all generations will call me blessed,

R.48: He has noticed me, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant, though I am not important. From now on, people of every time and place will say that I am blessed.

decisions.choice: low position: humble status, not humiliation
decisions.reason: The noun means a low and humble condition. Hannah prayed that God would look on her "affliction" (1 Samuel 1:11), using the same noun in the Greek. Mary is a young woman of no rank from an unknown village.

decisions.choice: slave: a woman who belongs to her master and is at his disposal
decisions.reason: The word is the feminine of the word for a slave (Philippians 2:7). Mary calls herself the Lord's slave: she belongs to him and puts herself at his command. Her place is that of one who belongs to a master, not of one in paid employment.

decisions.choice: call me blessed: declare me fortunate
decisions.reason: The verb is related to "blessed" in 1:45. Elizabeth was the first to do so.

decisions.choice: people of every time and place
decisions.reason: Readable explains "all generations".

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: ὅτι ἐποίησέν μοι μεγάλα ὁ δυνατός, καὶ ἅγιον τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ εἰς γενεὰς καὶ γενεὰς τοῖς φοβουμένοις αὐτόν.
records.gloss: Because did to me great things the Mighty [One], and holy the name of him, \v 50 and the mercy of him to generations and generations to the [ones] fearing him.
pieces: for the Mighty One has done great things for me. Holy is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name,
and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mercy reaches from one generation to the next for those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.49: because the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name,
L.50: and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mercy [is] for generations and generations to those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.49: God, the Mighty One, has done great things for me. His name is holy.
R.50: In every generation {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is kind to people who honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: holy is his name: God himself is holy
decisions.reason: In the Bible a name stands for the person (Psalm 111:9).

decisions.choice: his mercy for generations to those who fear him: Psalm 103:17
decisions.reason: Psalm 103:17 says the LORD's steadfast love is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him. "Mercy" in the Greek Old Testament often stands for God's faithful, covenant love.

decisions.choice: fear him: revere God and live in awe of him
decisions.reason: To fear God is to honor him and obey him (Proverbs 1:7). Readable says so.

decisions.choice: honor him and obey him
decisions.reason: "Fear" in modern English suggests terror. Readable gives the sense.

records.source: Ἐποίησεν κράτος ἐν βραχίονι αὐτοῦ, διεσκόρπισεν ὑπερηφάνους διανοίᾳ καρδίας αὐτῶν·
records.gloss: He did might with the arm of him, he scattered proud [ones] in [the] thought of heart of them;
pieces: He has acted with the strength of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arm; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has scattered the proud, with all the schemes of their hearts.

L.51: He has done mighty deeds with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arm; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has scattered [the] proud in [the] thought of their heart.

R.51: He has shown how strong {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is. He has scattered people who are proud and full of their own plans.

decisions.choice: his arm: God's power in action
decisions.reason: The arm of the LORD is a biblical picture for God's power, above all in rescuing Israel from Egypt (Deuteronomy 4:34; Psalm 89:11, 14; Isaiah 51:9).

decisions.choice: the proud in the thought of their heart: the arrogant, with their proud plans
alternatives: people who are proud in their heart, but not in their plans
decisions.reason: "In the thought of their heart" says where their pride lives and what it plans. God scatters them and their plans with them.

decisions.choice: he has shown ... scattered ... brought down: what God has done, seen as already done
alternatives: only past events in Israel's history
only what God will do in the future
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the aorist, the Greek tense for a completed act. Mary may be praising what God has always done for his people, or speaking of what he is now doing through her son as if it were already done, as the prophets did. Both readings are possible.

decisions.choice: schemes
decisions.reason: The noun is the thinking that plans and decides; with the proud it is their scheming.

records.source: καθεῖλεν δυνάστας ἀπὸ θρόνων καὶ ὕψωσεν ταπεινούς, πεινῶντας ἐνέπλησεν ἀγαθῶν καὶ πλουτοῦντας ἐξαπέστειλεν κενούς.
records.gloss: He brought down rulers from thrones and exalted lowly [ones], \v 53 hungry [ones] he filled with good things and being rich [ones] he sent away empty.
pieces: He has pulled the mighty down from their thrones and raised up the lowly.
The hungry {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has filled with good things, and the rich {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent away with nothing.

L.52: He has brought down rulers from [their] thrones and has lifted up [the] lowly;
L.53: [the] hungry {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has filled with good things, and [the] rich {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent away empty.

R.52: He has taken rulers off their thrones, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made humble people great.
R.53: He has given good things to hungry people, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent rich people away with nothing.

decisions.choice: God brings down and lifts up: Hannah's song again
decisions.reason: Hannah sang that God brings low and lifts up, that the full hire themselves out for bread while the hungry are satisfied (1 Samuel 2:5-8; compare Psalm 107:9; Job 5:11). God reverses human rank; Jesus says the same in 6:20-26.

decisions.choice: the lowly: the humble and poor, people of low rank
alternatives: only those who are humble in attitude
decisions.reason: The word is related to Mary's "low position" in 1:48. It describes people of low standing, who often were humble before God as well.

decisions.choice: the hungry ... good things: real hunger and real food, and more
decisions.reason: The poor of Israel went hungry; God feeds them (Psalm 146:7). In Luke the same reversal reaches to those hungry for God (6:21).

decisions.choice: he has shown ... scattered ... brought down: what God has done, seen as already done
alternatives: only past events in Israel's history
only what God will do in the future
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the aorist, the Greek tense for a completed act. Mary may be praising what God has always done for his people, or speaking of what he is now doing through her son as if it were already done, as the prophets did. Both readings are possible.

records.source: ἀντελάβετο Ἰσραὴλ παιδὸς αὐτοῦ, μνησθῆναι ἐλέους, καθὼς ἐλάλησεν πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν, τῷ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
records.gloss: He helped Israel servant of him, to remember mercy, \v 55 as he spoke to the fathers of us, to the Abraham and to the seed of him to the age.
pieces: He has come to the aid of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Israel and has not forgotten to show mercy,
as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to our ancestors, to Abraham and to his descendants forever."

L.54: He has helped Israel {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant, remembering mercy,
L.55: as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed forever."

R.54: He has helped Israel, the people who serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He has remembered to be kind to them,
R.55: just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised our ancestors. He promised to be kind to Abraham and to his family forever."

decisions.choice: Israel his servant: the title of Isaiah 41:8-9
decisions.reason: God calls Israel "my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, offspring of Abraham" (Isaiah 41:8). The servant here is the whole people; "servant" (a different word from "slave" in 1:48) can also mean child.

decisions.choice: remembering mercy ... to Abraham and his descendants forever
alternatives: as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his descendants
decisions.reason: "To Abraham and his descendants" can say whom God remembers in mercy, or whom he spoke to. The first is likelier: the promise was made to the fathers, and the mercy reaches Abraham's descendants forever (compare Micah 7:20). A rendering that keeps the Greek order leaves both open.

decisions.choice: remembering mercy: acting now on the mercy he promised
decisions.reason: When God "remembers" in Scripture, he acts on his promise (Genesis 8:1; Exodus 2:24; Psalm 98:3).

decisions.choice: his seed: Abraham's descendants
decisions.reason: "Seed" is a collective word for offspring (Genesis 17:7).

decisions.choice: our ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the forefathers of Israel, men and women. Literal keeps "fathers".

records.source: Ἔμεινεν δὲ Μαριὰμ σὺν αὐτῇ ὡς μῆνας τρεῖς, καὶ ὑπέστρεψεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: Remained then Mary with her about months three, and returned to the house of her.
pieces: Mary remained with Elizabeth about three months before returning home.

L.56: And Mary stayed with her about three months, and returned to her home.

R.56: Mary stayed with Elizabeth for about three months, and then went back home.

decisions.choice: about three months: until about the time Elizabeth's son was due
alternatives: Luke says she left before the birth
decisions.reason: Elizabeth was in her sixth month when Mary came (1:36), so three months brings them near the birth. Luke finishes Mary's part of the story before telling of John's birth; he does not say whether she stayed for it.

decisions.choice: Elizabeth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Elizabeth, since "her" could be unclear after the song.

records.source: Τῇ δὲ Ἐλισάβετ ἐπλήσθη ὁ χρόνος τοῦ τεκεῖν αὐτήν, καὶ ἐγέννησεν υἱόν.
records.gloss: To the then Elizabeth was fulfilled the time of the to give birth her, and she bore a son.
pieces: Elizabeth's time to give birth came, and she bore a son.

L.57: Now for Elizabeth the time was fulfilled for her to give birth, and she bore a son.

R.57: When the time came, Elizabeth had a baby boy.

decisions.choice: the time was fulfilled: the full time of her pregnancy had come
decisions.reason: Luke uses the language of fulfillment (compare 1:20, 23; 2:6). What the angel promised now happens.

records.heading: John is born and named

records.source: καὶ ἤκουσαν οἱ περίοικοι καὶ οἱ συγγενεῖς αὐτῆς ὅτι ἐμεγάλυνεν κύριος τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ μετ’ αὐτῆς, καὶ συνέχαιρον αὐτῇ.
records.gloss: And heard the neighbors and the relatives of her that magnified [the] Lord the mercy of him with her, and they were rejoicing with her.
pieces: Her neighbors and relatives heard how greatly the Lord had shown {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mercy to her, and they celebrated with her.

L.58: And her neighbors and relatives heard that [the] Lord had magnified {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mercy with her, and they rejoiced with her.

R.58: Her neighbors and relatives heard how very kind the Lord had been to her, and they were happy with her.

decisions.choice: magnified his mercy with her: showed her great mercy
decisions.reason: The verb Mary used for praising God (1:46) here has its plain sense, to make great: God's mercy to Elizabeth was great. The phrase echoes Genesis 19:19 in the Greek.

decisions.choice: they rejoiced with her: the joy promised in 1:14
decisions.reason: The angel said many would rejoice at John's birth (1:14). The verb can also mean "congratulate".

decisions.choice: how very kind the Lord had been to her
alternatives: the Lord had shown her great mercy
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for God's mercy here.

records.source: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ ἦλθον περιτεμεῖν τὸ παιδίον, καὶ ἐκάλουν αὐτὸ ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ Ζαχαρίαν.
records.gloss: And it came to pass on the day the eighth they came to circumcise the child, and they were calling it by the name of the father of him Zechariah.
pieces: When the child was eight days old, they came to circumcise him, and they wanted to give him his father's name, Zechariah.

L.59: And it happened on the eighth day [that] they came to circumcise the child, and they were calling him by the name of his father, Zechariah.

R.59: When the baby was eight days old, the family came together to circumcise him. They were going to name him Zechariah, after his father.

decisions.choice: on the eighth day: circumcision as the law commanded
alternatives: a family custom with no command behind it
decisions.reason: God commanded Abraham to circumcise every boy on the eighth day (Genesis 17:12; Leviticus 12:3), as the sign of his covenant. Naming the child at the same time is not commanded in the Old Testament, but Luke shows it was the custom (2:21).

decisions.choice: they were calling him: they were about to name him, or tried to
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense here shows an action begun but not completed: they were going to name him, until his mother stopped them.

decisions.choice: after his father: a common custom, though not a rule
alternatives: a rule that the first son take his father's name
decisions.reason: Children were often named after a father or grandfather. The neighbors expect it; Elizabeth refuses (1:60).

decisions.choice: they wanted to give him (B); they were going to name him (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the tense means.

records.source: καὶ ἀποκριθεῖσα ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ εἶπεν· Οὐχί, ἀλλὰ κληθήσεται Ἰωάννης.
records.gloss: And answering the mother of him said, No, but he will be called John.
pieces: But his mother answered, "No. His name is to be John."

L.60: And his mother answered and said, "No, but he will be called John."

R.60: But his mother said, "No! His name will be John."

decisions.choice: No, but he will be called John: Elizabeth insists on the name the angel gave
alternatives: a sudden choice of her own
decisions.reason: Luke does not say how Elizabeth knew the name; Zechariah could have written it to her. What matters is that both parents obey the angel's word (1:13).

records.source: καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτὴν ὅτι Οὐδείς ἐστιν ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας σου ὃς καλεῖται τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ.
records.gloss: And they said to her, No one is from the relatives of you who is called by the name this.
pieces: "But no one in your family is called by that name," they said to her.

L.61: And they said to her, "There is no one among your relatives who is called by this name."

R.61: The people said to her, "But no one in your family has that name!"

decisions.choice: no one among your relatives: a name normally came from the family
decisions.reason: The relatives expect a family name. A new name breaks with custom, and so marks the child as given by God for a new purpose.

records.source: ἐνένευον δὲ τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ τὸ τί ἂν θέλοι καλεῖσθαι αὐτό.
records.gloss: They were making signs then to the father of him the what - he might want to be called him.
pieces: Then they motioned to his father, asking what name he wanted the child to have.

L.62: And they made signs to his father [to ask] what he might want him to be called.

R.62: Then they made signs to Zechariah to ask him what he wanted to name the baby.

decisions.choice: made signs: they used gestures, as to someone who cannot hear
decisions.reason: They do not simply ask him. This suggests that he was deaf as well as mute (see 1:22).

decisions.choice: [to ask]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies what English needs to introduce the question.

records.source: καὶ αἰτήσας πινακίδιον ἔγραψεν λέγων· Ἰωάννης ἐστὶν ὄνομα αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And having asked for a writing tablet he wrote saying, John is name of him.
pieces: He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, "His name is John."

L.63: And asking for a writing tablet, he wrote, saying, "John is his name."

R.63: Zechariah asked for something to write on. Then he wrote, "His name is John."

decisions.choice: writing tablet: a small wooden board covered with wax
decisions.reason: Small tablets of wood coated with wax were used for notes; letters were scratched into the wax with a pointed tool.

decisions.choice: John is his name: a settled fact, not a proposal
decisions.reason: Zechariah writes in the present tense: the name has already been given, by God through the angel. He obeys at last (compare 1:20).

decisions.choice: something to write on
