decisions.reason: Readable avoids a word new readers may not know.

records.source: καὶ ἐθαύμασαν πάντες.
records.gloss: And marveled all.
pieces: Everyone was astonished.

decisions.choice: marveled: were astonished
decisions.reason: They are amazed that the parents agree on a name nobody expected. The wonder grows when Zechariah speaks (1:64-65).

records.gloss: Was opened then the mouth of him immediately and the tongue of him, and he was speaking blessing the God.
pieces: In that instant Zechariah's mouth was opened and his tongue loosed, and he began to speak, giving praise to God.

L.64: And immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue [freed], and he began to speak, blessing God.

R.64: Right away Zechariah could talk again, and he began to praise God.

decisions.choice: his mouth was opened and his tongue: one verb serves both nouns
decisions.reason: The Greek uses "was opened" for both; the tongue was set free to speak.

decisions.choice: was opened: God opened it
decisions.reason: The passive points to God. The silence ends at once, when Zechariah obeys the angel's word, as the angel said (1:20).

decisions.choice: blessing God: praising and thanking God
alternatives: giving God a blessing he lacks
decisions.reason: To "bless" God is to praise him with thanks. His first words are words of praise; 1:68 begins "Blessed be the Lord".

decisions.choice: giving praise to God (B); praise God (R)
decisions.reason: In English one blesses someone who needs a blessing. Balanced and Readable say "praise", and Literal keeps "blessing".

records.gloss: And came upon all fear the [ones] living around them, and in all the hill country of the Judea were being talked about all the words these, \v 66 and put all the [ones] having heard in the heart of them, saying, What then the child this will be?
pieces: Awe came over all their neighbors, and throughout the hill country of Judea people were talking about all these things.
Everyone who heard about them took them to heart and asked, "What then will this child turn out to be?"

L.65: And fear came upon all who lived around them, and in all the hill country of Judea all these words were being talked about,
L.66: and all who heard [them] laid [them] up in their heart, saying, "What then will this child be?"

R.65: All their neighbors were amazed, and filled with awe. People all through the hills of Judea were talking about what had happened.
R.66: Everyone who heard about it kept thinking about it. They asked, "What will this child become?"

decisions.choice: fear: awe at God's work
decisions.reason: As in 1:12 and 5:26, people react with holy fear when God acts.

decisions.choice: all these words: all these events
decisions.reason: The noun means word or matter, as in 1:37-38 and 2:15, 19. Here it is the whole story of the birth and the naming.

decisions.choice: laid them up in their heart: kept them in mind and thought about them
decisions.reason: A Hebrew-style way of saying they treasured and pondered the events (compare 2:19, 51; 1 Samuel 21:12).

decisions.choice: awe (B); amazed, and filled with awe (R)
decisions.reason: In modern English "fear" sounds like terror. Balanced and Readable say what kind of fear it is.

records.gloss: And for [the] hand of [the] Lord was with him.
pieces: For the Lord's hand was clearly with him.

L.66: For indeed [the] hand of [the] Lord was with him.

R.66: Everyone could see that the Lord was with him and was helping him.

decisions.choice: the hand of the Lord: God's power at work, guiding and protecting
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of God's power with his servants (Acts 11:21; Ezra 7:6).

decisions.choice: for the hand of the Lord was with him: Luke's own comment
alternatives: the end of what the people said
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends the people's question with a question mark and begins a new sentence. It explains why they asked: God's hand was plainly on the child. The comment covers John's whole life, as 1:80 goes on to show.

decisions.choice: clearly
decisions.reason: "And for" gives a strong reason: it was evident. Balanced says so with "clearly".

pieces: Then his father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke this prophecy:

L.67: And Zechariah his father was filled with [the] Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying,

R.67: Then John's father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit. He gave this message from God:

decisions.choice: prophesied: spoke a message from God by the Spirit
decisions.reason: To prophesy is to speak for God. Zechariah's song praises God, explains what he is doing, and says what the child will do.

decisions.choice: gave this message from God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what prophesying is.

records.heading: Zechariah blesses the God of Israel

records.source: Εὐλογητὸς κύριος ὁ θεὸς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, ὅτι ἐπεσκέψατο καὶ ἐποίησεν λύτρωσιν τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἤγειρεν κέρας σωτηρίας ἡμῖν ἐν οἴκῳ Δαυὶδ παιδὸς αὐτοῦ, καθὼς ἐλάλησεν διὰ στόματος τῶν ἁγίων ἀπ’ αἰῶνος προφητῶν αὐτοῦ, σωτηρίαν ἐξ ἐχθρῶν ἡμῶν καὶ ἐκ χειρὸς πάντων τῶν μισούντων ἡμᾶς, ποιῆσαι ἔλεος μετὰ τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν καὶ μνησθῆναι διαθήκης ἁγίας αὐτοῦ, ὅρκον ὃν ὤμοσεν πρὸς Ἀβραὰμ τὸν πατέρα ἡμῶν, τοῦ δοῦναι ἡμῖν ἀφόβως ἐκ χειρὸς ἐχθρῶν ῥυσθέντας λατρεύειν αὐτῷ ἐν ὁσιότητι καὶ δικαιοσύνῃ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ πάσαις ταῖς ἡμέραις ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: Blessed [be the] Lord the God of the Israel, because he visited and did redemption for the people of him, \v 69 and raised a horn of salvation for us in [the] house of David servant of him, \v 70 as he spoke through [the] mouth of the holy from [the] age prophets of him, \v 71 salvation from enemies of us and from [the] hand of all the [ones] hating us, \v 72 to do mercy with the fathers of us and to remember covenant holy of him, \v 73 [the] oath which he swore to Abraham the father of us, to give to us \v 74 fearlessly from [the] hand of enemies having been rescued to serve him \v 75 in holiness and righteousness before him all the days of us.
pieces: "Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has come to help {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people and set them free.
He has raised up a mighty power to save us in the house of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant David,
as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised long ago through the mouth of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy prophets:
salvation from our enemies and from the grip of all who hate us.
So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has shown the mercy promised to our ancestors and remembered {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy covenant,
the oath {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to our father Abraham: to grant us
that we, rescued from the hand of our enemies, might serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} without fear
in holiness and righteousness before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all our days.

L.68: "Blessed [be the] Lord, the God of Israel, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has visited and accomplished redemption for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people,
L.69: and has raised up a horn of salvation for us in [the] house of David {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant,
L.70: as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke through [the] mouth of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy prophets from of old,
L.71: salvation from our enemies and from [the] hand of all who hate us,
L.72: to show mercy to our fathers and to remember {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy covenant,
L.73: [the] oath that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to Abraham our father, to grant us
L.74: that, rescued from [the] hand of [our] enemies, [we might] serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} without fear
L.75: in holiness and righteousness before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all our days.

R.68: "Praise the Lord, the God of Israel! He has come to help {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people and has set them free.
R.69: He has given us a mighty king from the family of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant David, to save us.
R.70: Long ago {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised this through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy prophets.
R.71: He promised to save us from our enemies and from all who hate us.
R.72: He promised to be kind to our ancestors and to remember {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy covenant.
R.73: He made a promise with an oath to our father Abraham.
R.74: He promised to rescue us from our enemies, so that we could serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} without fear,
R.75: and live holy and righteous lives before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} every day we live.

decisions.choice: one sentence: a song of praise (1:68-75) built on God's promise
decisions.reason: Verses 68-75 are one long Greek sentence, in the style of Jewish blessings: "Blessed be God, because he has ...". A translation may break it into shorter sentences, but the line of thought is one: God has acted, as he promised, so that his people can serve him.

decisions.choice: visited: came to help
decisions.reason: When God "visits" his people in the Greek Old Testament, he comes to act for them (Genesis 50:24; Exodus 4:31; Ruth 1:6). The verb returns in 1:78 and 7:16.

decisions.choice: redemption: setting free, as God freed Israel from Egypt
decisions.reason: Redeeming is buying back or setting free. Israel hoped for God to redeem them (2:38; 24:21). Zechariah speaks first of rescue from enemies (1:71, 74), and then of the forgiveness of sins (1:77).

decisions.choice: a horn of salvation: a mighty Savior
decisions.reason: A horn is the strength of a wild ox, and so a picture of power (Deuteronomy 33:17). "The horn of my salvation" is God in Psalm 18:3; God promises to make a horn sprout for David (Psalm 132:17). Here it is the king from David's house: Jesus, not yet born.

decisions.choice: the covenant and the oath to Abraham: God's promise in Genesis 22:16-18
decisions.reason: God swore by himself to bless Abraham and his offspring and to give them victory over their enemies (Genesis 22:16-18; 26:3). Zechariah says the promise is now being kept.

decisions.choice: to show mercy to our fathers: to keep the promises made to them
alternatives: mercy to the dead ancestors themselves
decisions.reason: The ancestors received the promise; God shows them mercy by keeping it to their children (compare Micah 7:20).

decisions.choice: serve him: worship him
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for serving God in worship (2:37; Exodus 3:12). The goal of the rescue is free, unafraid worship.

decisions.choice: salvation: the same "salvation" as in 1:69, now explained
decisions.reason: The word picks up "horn of salvation" in 1:69 and says what it means: rescue from enemies.

decisions.choice: a mighty power to save us (B); a mighty king ... to save us (R)
decisions.reason: "Horn" means nothing to most English readers. Balanced keeps the sense of power; Readable names him a king, from the house of David.

decisions.choice: Praise the Lord
decisions.reason: "Blessed be" is church language. Readable uses the everyday word, as in 1:64.

decisions.choice: has come to help his people and set them free
alternatives: has visited and accomplished redemption for his people
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of "visited" and "redemption" in plain English. Literal keeps the words.

records.source: καὶ σὺ δέ, παιδίον, προφήτης Ὑψίστου κληθήσῃ, προπορεύσῃ γὰρ ἐνώπιον κυρίου ἑτοιμάσαι ὁδοὺς αὐτοῦ, τοῦ δοῦναι γνῶσιν σωτηρίας τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ ἐν ἀφέσει ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν, διὰ σπλάγχνα ἐλέους θεοῦ ἡμῶν, ἐν οἷς ἐπισκέψεται ἡμᾶς ἀνατολὴ ἐξ ὕψους, ἐπιφᾶναι τοῖς ἐν σκότει καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου καθημένοις, τοῦ κατευθῦναι τοὺς πόδας ἡμῶν εἰς ὁδὸν εἰρήνης.
records.gloss: And you and, child, prophet of Most High will be called, you will go before for before [the] Lord to prepare ways of him, \v 77 to give knowledge of salvation to the people of him in forgiveness of sins of them, \v 78 through [the] inward parts of mercy of God of us, in which will visit us [the] rising from on high, \v 79 to shine on the [ones] in darkness and shadow of death sitting, to direct the feet of us into [the] way of peace.
pieces: And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High, for you will go ahead of the Lord to prepare {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways,
to make known to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people the salvation that comes through the forgiveness of their sins.
Because our God is full of tender mercy, the dawn from on high will visit us,
to give light to those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death, and to direct our steps onto the road of peace."

L.76: And you also, child, will be called a prophet of [the] Most High, for you will go before [the] Lord to prepare {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways,
L.77: to give knowledge of salvation to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people in [the] forgiveness of their sins,
L.78: through [the] tender mercy of our God, by which [the] dawn from on high will visit us,
L.79: to shine on those sitting in darkness and [the] shadow of death, to guide our feet into [the] way of peace."

R.76: And you, my child, will be called a prophet of God Most High. You will go ahead of the Lord to get the way ready for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.77: You will tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people how they can be saved by having their sins forgiven.
R.78: Our God is very kind and full of love. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make a new day dawn for us from heaven,
R.79: to shine on people who live in darkness, in the shadow of death. It will guide us on the road to peace."

decisions.choice: go before the Lord to prepare his ways: Malachi 3:1 and Isaiah 40:3
alternatives: a general call to get ready
decisions.reason: God promised to send his messenger to prepare the way before him (Malachi 3:1), and a voice crying, "Prepare the way of the Lord" (Isaiah 40:3; Luke 3:4). "The Lord" here is God, as in 1:16-17; Luke's readers know that he comes in Jesus (1:43).

decisions.choice: in the forgiveness of their sins: salvation consists in forgiveness, or comes through it
alternatives: forgiveness as a separate gift alongside salvation
decisions.reason: The salvation John announces is not first a rescue from Rome but the forgiveness of sins (3:3). The rescue from enemies of 1:71 is now seen at its root.

decisions.choice: the tender mercy of our God: God's heartfelt compassion
decisions.reason: The first noun is the inner parts of the body, thought of as the seat of the feelings, as many languages speak of the heart. With "mercy" it means deep, heartfelt compassion.

decisions.choice: the dawn from on high: the rising light that comes from God, the coming king
decisions.reason: The noun means the rising of the sun or a star, the dawn. In the Greek Old Testament it also translates "Branch", a name for the coming king from David's line (Jeremiah 23:5; Zechariah 3:8; 6:12). The next verse, about shining on those in darkness, shows that light is the main picture here (Isaiah 9:2; 60:1-3; Malachi 4:2).

decisions.choice: will visit us, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: has visited us, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have the past tense, as in 1:68. Several early manuscripts have the future. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death: Isaiah 9:2 and Psalm 107:10
decisions.reason: Isaiah 9:2 promises that a people walking in darkness will see a great light, living in the land of the shadow of death. Matthew quotes it of Jesus (Matthew 4:16).

decisions.choice: the way of peace: the path that leads to peace with God and the wholeness he gives
decisions.reason: Peace in the Bible is the whole well-being God gives. The song ends where the angels' song will begin (2:14).

decisions.choice: make known to his people the salvation (B); tell his people how they can be saved (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say the same in plain English.

decisions.choice: make a new day dawn for us from heaven
alternatives: the dawn from on high will visit us
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of the sunrise and says it comes from God.

records.source: Τὸ δὲ παιδίον ηὔξανε καὶ ἐκραταιοῦτο πνεύματι, καὶ ἦν ἐν ταῖς ἐρήμοις ἕως ἡμέρας ἀναδείξεως αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὸν Ἰσραήλ.
records.gloss: The and child was growing and was becoming strong in spirit, and he was in the deserted [places] until [the] day of showing of him to the Israel.
pieces: As the child grew, he became strong in spirit, and he lived in the desert places until the day he showed himself to Israel.

L.80: And the child kept growing and becoming strong in spirit, and he was in the wilderness until [the] day of his public appearance to Israel.

R.80: The child grew up and became strong in spirit. He lived in the desert until the time came for him to begin his work among the people of Israel.

decisions.choice: strong in spirit: strong in his inner life, which God's Spirit filled
alternatives: strong in the Holy Spirit (with a capital S)
decisions.reason: The phrase most naturally means John's own spirit, as in 2:40 of Jesus. But John was filled with the Holy Spirit from birth (1:15), so the two cannot be separated.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: the dry, lonely land, probably near the Jordan and the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: John's preaching begins in the wilderness (3:2-3). The wilderness was where God met Israel after the exodus, and where the prophets expected a new beginning (Isaiah 40:3).

decisions.choice: public appearance: the day he was shown to Israel and began his work
decisions.reason: The noun was used for the public installation of an official. John's public work begins in 3:1-2.

decisions.choice: until the time came for him to begin his work among the people of Israel
alternatives: until the day of his public appearance to Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says what his public appearance was.
